Notes: Fixed so every run is reproducible. Change it to see sampling variation, not to shop for a better answer.

Number of savings groups. Sized so the pool lands in the tens of millions - the warehouse band from LIT-011 and LIT-012. A pool small enough for fixed costs to dominate produces a degenerate model, which is itself the OQ-2 finding.
Poisson mean. Roughly a third to a half of a 20-30 member group borrowing in a given cycle.
Lognormal mean. Placeholder - not calibrated to any observed distribution.
Lognormal shape. Produces a right-skewed book, which is what small-ticket lending looks like.
Cycle-bound lending: most loans mature inside one savings cycle.
Dispersion around the mean term.
Flat service charge, not declining balance - the convention in most VSLA methodologies.
Baseline annual probability of default per loan. PLACEHOLDER - see the calibration note.
Share of defaulted principal eventually recovered, largely via group joint liability.
Early repayment. Material for short-tenor assets.
Pairwise default correlation within a geography. THE parameter that matters most - see the sensitivity note.
Distinct regions. Fewer regions means more concentration for a given pool size.
Multi-originator pooling per LIT-008 and LIT-011.
Senior tranche as a share of the pool.
Mezzanine tranche.
First-loss / junior tranche. The 10-20% working range comes from LIT-013 and LIT-015.
Senior note coupon.
Mezzanine coupon.
Servicing. Likely higher per dollar than any comparable deal for community-originated assets.
Legal, rating, listing, structuring. The fixed-cost term that actually drives minimum viable pool size (OQ-2).
Monte Carlo paths. Lower than ideal, traded against runtime on a pool of this size in pure Python. Enough for a stable mean; read the p99 as indicative.
